subject.title: [Bug]: In msteams channel messages, OpenClaw can't access inbound attachments

question: Should the Microsoft Teams plugin recover channel/group inbound file attachments by enabling the narrowed text/html Graph fallback by default, or require an explicit opt-in config gate for Graph message fetches?
rationale: Current docs already describe Graph-enabled channel media, but the fallback changes when Teams messages request Graph tokens and message fetches; automation cannot choose that operational policy for maintainers.

options.title: Accept the narrowed default fallback
options.body: Merge the plugin-owned fix once exact-head checks are acceptable, using the text/html stub as the existing Teams signal for Graph media recovery.

options.title: Require an opt-in Graph fetch gate
options.body: Ask the PR to add a documented config flag if maintainers want high-volume deployments to opt in before ordinary text/html stubs trigger Graph lookup.

options.title: Pause for more tenant variants
options.body: Hold the fix until maintainers see fresh proof for group chat, private/shared channel, and permission-denied variants on the same head.

recommendation.title: Accept the narrowed default fallback
recommendation.body: Merge the plugin-owned fix once exact-head checks are acceptable, using the text/html stub as the existing Teams signal for Graph media recovery.

likelyOwner.reason: His history spans the Microsoft Teams plugin boundary and attachment/security flow, making him the best available routing owner for the default-vs-config policy choice.
